# Revised Summary

Mexico's security cabinet stated that two US citizens killed in a car crash during an anti-narcotics operation were not "authorised" to operate on Mexican territory, with one having entered as a visitor and the other on a diplomatic passport, yet neither possessed formal accreditation for operational activities. Following President Sheinbaum's ordered investigation, Mexico's security ministry asserted that federal authorities had not been informed of the agents' presence—a disclosure that raises unresolved questions about what operational activities they were conducting, under whose direction, and whether their deaths occurred during authorized or unauthorized operations. The source reports the vehicle's crash and explosion following a raid on suspected drug labs but is silent on whether Mexican federal authorities were conducting the raid independently, whether the US agents were embedded with Mexican operatives, or the nature of any coordination that may have preceded the fatal operation. The stated absence of formal accreditation and notification creates an ambiguity: whether these agents were operating entirely outside official channels or whether official US-Mexican protocols themselves were bypassed.
